_comment: Hand-written reference verdicts. NOT generated by the engine.
Each entry was derived from the specification, the cryptographic literature
or a first-principles argument about the Dolev-Yao model, and is recorded in
DECISIONS.md. test_reference.py compares the engine against this file;
regression_snapshot.json is the generated file and is never the oracle.
Do not edit this file to match engine output -- add a DECISIONS.md entry.
model_assumptions: D1: a claim is evaluated only over traces whose CLAIMANT run has an honest
agent and an honest peer. Other runs may involve the attacker.
D2: perfect cryptography; an attacker either can or cannot build a term.
D3: at most one run per role (Bounds.max_runs_per_role = 1).

ns.source: literature: Lowe 1996 'Authentication and key exchange via a highly insecure public channel'
reasoning: Alice's run is honest (agent and peer), so Mallory never holds a key that
opens Na or Nb: I1/I2 are VERIFIED.
Lowe's man in the middle gives Mallory a run of Alice with peer M, so
Mallory decrypts Na from message 1 and Nb from message 3, while Bob's
run (peer Alice, honest) completes via a forged message 3.
That trace breaks R1 (Secret ni), R2 (Secret nr), R3 (Niagree: Bob's
partner is M, not Bob's initiator) and R4 (Nisynch: {I,na}pk(R) is not
{I,na}pk(M)).

nsl.source: literature: Lowe 1996 (the NSL fix); spec section 10 'NSL: all claims VERIFIED'
reasoning: NSL differs from NS only by adding R (the responder's identity) to
message 2: {R,ni,nr}pk(I).
Consequently an Alice-with-Mallory run cannot accept Bob's message 2:
her recv_2 resolves R to M while Bob's send_2 resolves it to Bob, so the
relay fails and Alice's run cannot complete with Mallory as her peer.
Mallory therefore never receives {Nb}pk(M) and never learns Nb; and she
never sees Na in the clear either, because the only Alice runs that can
complete are ones with an honest peer.
Hence all eight claims hold.
R1 needs the D1 argument: Mallory CAN run Alice with peer M and learn
Na, but such a run makes R1 vacuous only for Alice's own claims. For Bob
the claimant run is Bob's (honest, peer Alice). In every trace where Bob
completes, either Mallory never learned Na (Alice ran with Bob) or Bob
did not complete. Verified exhaustively over 654 states.

challenge_response.source: reasoned: every message is sealed under the pairwise key k(A,B), which the attacker cannot obtain
reasoning: A1 (Secret na): Alice's run is honest; na is inside {A,na}k(A,B), which
only Alice and Bob can open. VERIFIED.
A2 (Alive): Alice's recv_2 is {B,na}k(A,B). The attacker cannot build it
without k(A,B), so if Alice completes, a Bob run produced it. VERIFIED.
A3/A4: that Bob run is mutually paired (agent/peer swap) and the messages
are byte-identical. VERIFIED.
B1 (Alive): Bob's recv_1 needs k(A,B) as well. VERIFIED.
B2 (Nisynch): the corresponding Alice run is mutually paired. VERIFIED.
NOTE: adding the attacker's own constants nM/kM (Issue 3) does not change
any of these, because the obstacle is the PAIRWISE key between two honest
agents, which attacker constants cannot help with. See DECISIONS.md D6.

challenge_response_no_id.source: reasoned: the reply is the bare nonce in the clear, so a passive attacker learns it
reasoning: The reply is send_2(B,A, na) with no encryption and no responder
identity. Mallory relays the session and reads na off the wire.
A1 (Secret na) FALSIFIED: the plaintext reply is in her knowledge at the
end of Alice's run.
A2/A3/A4 are VERIFIED *because of D1*: Mallory can only answer Alice's
recv_2 when Alice's run has Mallory as its peer, and D1 restricts the
claimant's peer to honest agents. Within the search space Alice always
talks to Bob, who completes, so Alive/Niagree/Nisynch hold.
This is a model consequence, not an engine accident: without D1 these
three would be FALSIFIED, and NS's I3/I4 would be FALSIFIED too, which
contradicts spec section 10. See DECISIONS.md D7.
B1 (Alive): Bob's recv_1 needs k(A,B), so a Bob run implies an Alice run
exists. VERIFIED.
B2 (Nisynch): that Alice run is mutually paired. VERIFIED.

replay.source: reasoned: the single message {A,na} is public and carries no freshness
reasoning: Message 1 is {A,na} in the clear, so Mallory can produce it at will.
A1 (Niagree) and A2 (Nisynch): Alice's run is honest (peer B), she sends
and completes immediately, and there is nothing that forces Bob to run.
A trace in which only Alice runs therefore exists, and it falsifies both
agreement claims. FALSIFIED.
B1 (Niagree) and B2 (Nisynch): Mallory forges {A,na} into Bob's recv_1
without any Alice run existing at all, so Bob completes with no
corresponding initiator. FALSIFIED.
This is precisely the defect the example exists to show.
NOTE: the review brief expected some of these to be VERIFIED; see
DECISIONS.md D8.

yahalom.source: reasoned: a four-message session whose first message is sealed under k(A,B)
reasoning: A1 (Secret na): the first message {A,na}k(A,B) is under the pairwise key,
so Mallory cannot read it. VERIFIED.
A2/A3: completing Alice's run requires the reply {na}k(A,B) from a Bob
run, which is mutually paired. VERIFIED.
B1/B2: symmetrically, completing Bob's run requires an Alice run. VERIFIED.
This example is the secure baseline for the agreement machinery; the
falsification paths are covered by ns and replay.
